1.explanation:
The file src/languages/perl.js contains the Perl language definition for highlight.js, including the rules that detect regex literals and the match operator variants (m//, qr//, etc.). Since the bug is about arbitrary delimiters for m// and qr// not being recognized, this is the primary file where the regex‐parsing modes need to be enhanced to accept any non-alphanumeric delimiter. No other language files are involved, as this is specific to Perl’s syntax.  

If highlight.js’s generic regex handling were insufficient, one might also look at src/lib/regex.js, but in this case all of Perl’s delimiter logic lives in perl.js and should be updated there.

2.explanation: All of Perl’s custom regex‐parsing logic lives in src/languages/perl.js. That file defines how the m//, qr//, qq//, etc., operators are detected and highlighted. Currently it only handles simple slash-delimited regexes and doesn’t implement the full set of arbitrary delimiters (|, #, {, (, <, etc.). To fix the bug, perl.js needs to be updated to parse and highlight m and qr operators with any valid Perl delimiter.
2.bug_scenario: In Perl code the “m” match operator with arbitrary delimiters (for example m(/$); or m|/$|, m{/$}, m#/$#) is not being recognized as a regex by highlight.js. In the screenshot you see that $d !~ m(/$); fails to highlight “/$” as a regex; highlight.js treats the slash literally rather than parsing the m operator with its delimiters. The same gap occurs for qr(...) and other Regexp Quote Like Operators.
